reasons: A has a persistent New task (required) label and explicitly states An empty title deletes this task. in both desktop and phone editing screenshots, supporting understanding of consequential editing behavior.

A places filters before the task list, retaining visible navigation in long mixed/editing views; B offers a stronger solid selected state and wider phone filter targets at the bottom. These are offsetting navigation strengths.

Both variants preserve readable wrapped long text, visible row actions, redundant completion cues, clear Save/Cancel, restrained TodoMVC branding and visible author/project credits. Neither shows a major visual usability failure.
A wins narrowly on task-supporting information; title alignment and other stylistic preferences were not treated as functional evidence.

criteriaEvidence.A: 3: Distinct completion ticks/strikethroughs, readable mixed-language and long titles, persistent row actions, filters above tasks.
criteriaEvidence.B: 3: Same strong task readability and completion cues; solid red filter selection is especially easy to identify, though navigation follows the list.

criteriaEvidence.A: 3: Stable field label and separated toolbar/list/footer; phone toolbar is somewhat dense and some row actions wrap below short text.
criteriaEvidence.B: 3: Compact input and separately grouped bulk action/footer filters; consistent row divisions, with some empty space from wrapped phone actions.

criteriaEvidence.criterion: 内容与动作对任务支持
criteriaEvidence.A: 4: Explicit Add/Edit/Delete/Save/Cancel and navigation, plus persistent input label and in-context empty-title deletion warning in both editing sizes.
criteriaEvidence.B: 3: All core action labels visible and Mark all complete is clear; no visible empty-title deletion warning and only placeholder identification for the new input.

criteriaEvidence.A: 3: No visible horizontal overflow or action/text collision; full-width editor, wrapped controls, filters before list; actual touch hit areas unverified.
criteriaEvidence.B: 3: No visible overflow or action/text collision; wide three-part footer filters and full-width editor; navigation shifts down with list length and hit areas unverified.

criteriaEvidence.A: 3: Approximately 800px centered card, aligned text/actions, complete long text and credits within 900px viewport.
criteriaEvidence.B: 3: Approximately 760px centered card with similarly readable lines, stable action alignment and complete mixed/editing content within viewport.

criteriaEvidence.A: 3: Consistent restrained branding, buttons and structure; empty state omits irrelevant editing help; completed text gets more muted during editing.
criteriaEvidence.B: 3: Consistent restrained branding, buttons and structure; empty state still includes editing help with no tasks; completed text gets more muted during editing.

coverage.method: Individually inspected every original-resolution screenshot through view_image; no browser interaction.

limitations: Static visual judgment only; no add/edit/cancel/complete/filter/delete/clear-all-completed execution was verified.
Actual touch hit areas, keyboard/focus behavior, accessibility semantics, scrolling below captured bounds, virtual-keyboard layout and in-memory Store semantics remain unknown.
No Completed-only, all-completed, validation-error or unbroken-long-text state was supplied or inspected.
Phone mixed/editing screenshots place credits below the captured viewport; this is not evidence that credits were removed.
A narrow visual preference does not establish functional correctness.
